Measured against the live export and the source at 329a074, plus git history of /home/ajs7/project/reflow2.","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28.

① OBSERVED. 354 of 763 TemporalFacts have no HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT edge, although every subject_id resolves. 4 have the edge from a node other than their subject_id. flow:release-cut's exit_point names step 8 of 9. Expected: record_finding draws the edge (temporal_tools.rs, "the subject carries the fact"). NOT affected: 405 facts have the edge from their own subject.

② PRECEDENT. fact:defect-a-property-naming-a-node-is-unguarded-while-edges-are-not (2026-08-16) recorded a TemporalFact written through create_node, which sets subject_id and draws no edge. fact:which-properties-are-node-references-is-a-judgement-made-once-and-never-recorded-for-the-others (2026-08-29) recorded that subject_id and Snapshot.target_id need different answers. ver:the-release-cut-reads-back-whole verified the cut at EIGHT steps.

③ CANDIDATES.
- C1: writers that set subject_id and draw no edge.
- C2: facts written before record_finding drew the edge.
- C3: edges drawn, then lost to a delete, merge or rename.
- C4: the observation is wrong.

④⑤ MEASURED, by writer and by date (record_finding arrived in aa799bd on 2026-09-07, drawing the edge from the start).
- Non-manual facts dated before 09-07: 275 of 326 (84%) have no edge. The 51 that do had it drawn by hand. That is C2, and the writer of that era was the generic create_node, so C1 as well.
- Dated from 09-07: 275 have the edge and 22 do not. 21 of the 22 are dated 09-07 to 09-09, the tool's first days, and one is dated 09-26: create_node is still a live route to an edgeless fact.
- report_manual_work (manual_work.rs:110-138) sets subject_id to the Project and NEVER draws the edge. All 46 manual-work facts lack it, 27 of them written after 09-07. A LIVE writer defect.
- C3 is not needed to explain any count and was not separately measured.
- C4: the counts come from the full sorted export, the same document the CI gate imports.
The 4 mismatches date from the create_node era (08-09 to 08-27) and no snapshot of an earlier subject_id exists. In 2 of them the statement names BOTH nodes, so the second node was hung on deliberately. HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT has in practice carried both "the subject carries this" and "this also concerns that", the job ABOUT_ENTITY was declared for.
The flow: add_flow sets entry_point and exit_point once. part_of_flow adds steps and never touches them. flow_report (flow.rs:217, 274) serves the pointers beside the step_order it sorts by, so the report shows two answers. Capability.is_entry_point and is_exit_point are written by add_capability (capture.rs:1797) and read by NOTHING in core.

⑥ CLASS. The instance is whichever writer forgot. The cause is that the second copy of a stored twin is maintained BY EACH WRITER, BY HAND, with nothing checking it. Fixing record_finding would not have prevented the create_node facts, the manual-work facts or the flow, and fixing report_manual_work would not prevent the next writer. So the fix belongs where every writer passes: the schema declares the twin and its authority, the store keeps the derived copy on every write, a repair brings existing designs into line and reports each repair, and a check fails on drift.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
- why each of the 4 mismatches was drawn (no history survives)
- whether the dimension and readiness twins drift in designs that hold those types (this one holds none)
- whether other writers (tools/migrate_backlog.py, imports) contributed","subject_id":"req:a-relation-stored-in-more-than-one-place-has-one-authoritative-copy-and-no-copy-drifts-unnoticed","valid_from":"2026-09-28"}
